cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic strip-woven kente cloth with the checkerboard pattern and geometric weft motifs characteristic of Ashanti weaving traditions, matching both the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man's garment composed of 25 hand woven narrow strips of European imported cotton and silk or rayon, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled alternately to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. All have a uniform warp design with two groups of three white warp stripes against on a black background. The weft has double-blocks of lines of varying colour (using a second pair of heddles) that frame discontinuous weft abstract geometrical zig-zag and geometrically shaped patterns in red, yellow, green, blue and black silk/rayon. The warp ends have not been hemmed.
